newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia's AgriBank urged to aid food security plan.
newsitem.headline: Namibia's AgriBank urged to aid food security plan.

text.p: The Agricultural Bank of Namibia would have to intensify efforts to broaden its services to help the country meet its aim for food self-sufficiency, Agriculture minister Helmuth Angula said on Wednesday night.

"Seventy percent of our people are engaged in farming in one way or another", he said, "therefore we need to ensure that all farming sectors have access to financial institutions to stimulate production and self-sufficiency at household level".
"This will aid efforts by the Southern African Development Community to achieve food security at regional and country level."

Angula said the Agricultural Bank of Namibia, which had in the past catered mainly for the commercial farmer, would have to intensify its efforts to extend its services to the communal or emerging farmers.
"The bank should go to the people, not expect people to come and find it in Windhoek," he said.
Agriculture is one of the mainstays of the Namibian economy, alongside mining, fishing and tourism, but has suffered severe setbacks due to recurring droughts.
